metadata.scenario: Backtest: WeWork's 2019 IPO attempt, evaluated on S-1 disclosures as of August 2019

sources.claim: Peak private valuation $47B (January 2019 SoftBank round); marketed valuation collapsed below $10B during the IPO process
SoftBank $9.5B rescue package (October 2019): $5B new financing + $1.5B acceleration + $3B tender offer
Adam Neumann super-voting shares, leased buildings he owned to WeWork, trademarked 'We' and licensed it to the company for $5.9M
Neumann sold over $700M in personal stock before the IPO
Airbnb priced its IPO at $68 per share on 2020-12-09 and nearly doubled on debut
Blue Apron cut its IPO price from the $15-17 range to $10 (2017-06-29) and had never posted a profitable quarter

properties.structural_mismatch: long-term leases funded by short-term memberships

precedents.scenario: Airbnb entered its 2020 IPO with $4.8B revenue (2019) and a $674M net loss — about 14% of revenue — with conventional governance and no founder self-dealing disclosures.
precedents.reasoning: Losses were a manageable share of revenue and governance was clean; the IPO priced at $68 and nearly doubled on debut.

precedents.scenario: Blue Apron went public in 2017 having never posted a profitable quarter, and had to cut its IPO price from the $15-17 range down to $10 amid persistent losses.
precedents.reasoning: Chronic losses with no path to profitability destroyed pricing power; the stock kept falling after the downgraded debut.

documents: WeWork S-1 excerpt (financials): for the year ended December 31, 2018, the company reported revenue of approximately $1.82 billion and a net loss of approximately $1.61 billion — a loss equal to roughly 88% of revenue. The company was last valued privately at $47 billion in January 2019.

WeWork S-1 excerpt (governance): CEO Adam Neumann held super-voting shares giving him control over shareholder decisions. Disclosure items included leasing buildings he partly owned to the company, trademarking the word 'We' and licensing it to the company for $5.9 million, and personal stock sales of over $700 million prior to the IPO.

WeWork S-1 excerpt (business model): the company signs long-term leases (average 15 years) while selling short-term memberships, creating a structural asset-liability duration mismatch. Post-IPO-process, the marketed valuation collapsed below $10 billion, the IPO was withdrawn, and SoftBank assembled a $9.5 billion rescue at a valuation near $8 billion.
request_zh: 请评估 WeWork 在 2019 年是否应获准推进 IPO。必须基于图谱证据、历史先例和政策检查，并记录唯一的最终决定。
